surfaces.part: lower sandbag courses (repeated gray top over brown front, 12-row period)

answer.evidence: The column at x=8 shows gray rows 1-6 ending in a light 2-row edge line at rows 7-8, followed by about 10 rows of brown front face (rows 9-18). The same pattern repeats every 12 rows (edge lines at 19-20, 31-32, 40-41), and the gray bulges at x=4 and x=11 show the same top-then-front rhythm for each bag. The first course has a distinct top band of about 6 rows with an edge line and a front face well over 3 rows. The lower courses are partly overlapped by the course above, so each of them shows only a shorter top strip. The object has no isometric side face and is not a flat slab, so it reads as a 3/4 view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small narrow column of stacked sandbags, not a whole building, so it does not match the reference kind. Judged by eye against the references, it has about 4 lightness steps per bag with a tinted dark-brown outline. Measured facts: 8 visible tones per tile against 10-12 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edges, so the outline is not near-black. Each bag has a bulge highlight and a dark underside, but there is little grain or speckle, and the material ramps are shallower than the roof tiles and stone in the references. It is clean and not a sticker, but it is a little thinner and flatter than the Beodeul reference. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: repeated sandbag courses (same gray top, light edge, brown face)

answer.evidence: The object is a tall strip of stacked bag courses that repeat about every 12 rows. At x=8, rows 1-6 are a gray top surface that ends in a light 2-row edge line at rows 7-8, with a brown front face below at rows 9-18. The same sequence repeats at rows 19-20, 31-32 and 40-41. At x=11, rows 1-2 are light, 3-6 dark gray, then light again at 7-8. The silhouette bulges from width 15 to 16 and narrows again every 12 rows, which gives the rounded bag tops. The bottom has a brown front face of about 5 rows (rows 42-46) over a dark base row at 47. The top of each bag is only a few rows deep, but the main body shows a top band with a front-edge line and a front face of 3+ rows, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical stack of sandbags, roughly one tile wide and two tall. It is a prop rather than a full building, so the reference kind is only loosely comparable. The measured facts show 8 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, with 0% near-flat coverage, which matches the references. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted brown, the dark tone of the adjacent material, not a black sticker line. Texture is limited to the bag-to-bag shading, with no grain or speckle dots as on the reference plaster and tiles. It is slightly thinner than the references but not flat or sticker-like, and a careful artist would likely accept it as a small prop.
